errors: Says SQLite will not enforce the users foreign key so the bad order row stays; better-sqlite3 enables foreign keys by default, so the insert itself rejects
R1-A.why: Accurate, well-ranked findings with the premise question and defaults, but the existing warehouse users, rollback, migrations and a testable launch gate are missing, and the plan carries some generic extras (pentest, 3x load test, state machine, privacy) that dilute a one-month scope.

errors: Claims the order row stays behind for an unknown userId; with better-sqlite3's default foreign-key enforcement the insert rejects instead
R1-B.why: Strong grounding, safe defaults that change the plan, a Phase 0 with backup-and-restore and tests, per-phase checks, a go/no-go list and a revert rule; lacks a migration approach and does not plan the staff-auth rollout around the warehouse workflow.

errors: States the order row is already inserted before the crash for an unknown userId; better-sqlite3 enforces foreign keys by default, so the insert rejects
R1-C.why: Thorough and correctly ordered with failing-tests-first and migrations plus tested backups, but backups sit in week 3, there is no rollback or warehouse-compatibility step, the launch gate is only a rehearsal, and it accumulates checklist items (helmet, Sentry, UUIDs, indexes).

R1-D.why: Concise, factually clean and proportionate, with a done-when test for every item, SPF/DKIM and the sender placeholder caught, and explicit deferrals; weaker on migrations, backup-before-change, rollback and how the warehouse is kept working during the auth change.

errors: Asserts the foreign key is not enforced because db.js never sets the pragma; better-sqlite3 turns foreign keys on by default
Schedules backups in phase 3, after the phase 2 schema changes, with no migration mechanism for the new column and table
R1-E.why: Very actionable: concrete first steps that confirm the crash before fixing, staff auth chosen to fit existing clients, per-step checks, go/no-go and pause triggers; let down by the foreign-key assertion and by schema changes landing before backups or a migration approach.

R1-F.why: Correct findings, sensible week-by-week order, explicit deferrals and an order of sacrifice, but the steps are thinner on verification (no per-step checks or launch gate), with no rollback, migration approach or protection for the current warehouse workflow.

errors: Says the insert succeeds for a missing user because SQLite foreign keys are off; better-sqlite3 enables them by default
Describes only a hung request; on current Node the unhandled rejection also terminates the process
R1-G.why: Best treatment of the premise after H (cheaper tracking-token path, keep it off the internet until the gate passes), with per-phase checks, a go/no-go list and soft-launch revert triggers; its default path (direct customer access plus a products table) is the costly one, and migrations and backup-before-schema-change are missing.

errors: Says a JSON body sent to the import 'crashes it'; that throw is synchronous, so Express returns a 500 and the process survives
R1-H.why: The only plan that treats the warehouse as a live constraint (log-mode staff auth with a revert switch, backup before a user_version migration, restore check) while picking the cheapest safe default, flagging its own uncertain claim with a command to settle it, and giving first steps and a concrete launch gate.
